svg.text: What B learned from 2019-2023 is still measurable in later returns
How similarly two Taiwanese stocks respond to the residual moves of the 30 US stocks.
Left: measured from returns after the model was fixed. Right: read off the trained model. Same layout, same colour scale.
2024-12-26 to 2025-12-30, not used in training or selection
Mean correlation between two stocks' profiles
Agreement over all 1,225 stock pairs (Mantel r): +0.34 in fold 1, +0.43 in fold 2, p < 0.001 in both.
Reference: same period as training +0.67 / +0.64; market structure itself, training vs test period +0.46 / +0.57.
Fold 2 repeats this on an earlier split: fit up to 2022-12, measured on 2023-12-20 to 2024-12-25.
Industry separation (same minus different industry), measured / learned: fold 1 +0.27 / +0.30, fold 2 +0.33 / +0.23, all p <= 0.002.
Per stock, the learned and measured profiles are positively correlated for 38/50 (fold 1) and 42/50 (fold 2) stocks.
Estimator check: a multivariate ridge instead of pairwise correlations gives the same structure (r = +0.90 / +0.91, training window).
Left: correlation of each Taiwanese stock's return on day t with each US stock's return on the previous shared trading day, both net of their market's daily mean.
Right: columns of B, which starts at zero; industry labels never enter training. Cells average over all cross-pairs of the two industries.
Industries with n >= 2 shown (9 of 18); Cement and Electronic Components are one pair each. Zero-volume Taiwan non-trading days are excluded.
